images.title: A line of 4 cm 6 mm on a ruler
images.purpose: Show how a length is read in cm and mm: a line from 0 that passes the 4 cm mark and ends on the 6th small mark, 4 cm 6 mm = 46 mm.
images.composition: A ruler from 0 to 6 cm with a thick teal line above it and a read-out at the bottom.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. RULER: one yellow rectangle 1080 px wide and 110 px high (x 188 to 1268, y 360 to 470), 180 px for each cm, with exactly 61 tick marks, one every 18 px (1 mm), of which 7 are long (60 px) at every cm and numbered below in 40 px 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6, 6 are medium (45 px) at the 5 mm marks, and the other 48 short (30 px). LINE: one teal #0072B2 line 14 px thick from x 188 to x 1016 at y 300 with a round end dot of 28 px at x 1016, and a thin dashed vertical line from the dot down to the ruler at x 1016. BRACKETS: one amber #E69F00 bracket under the ruler from x 908 (the 4 cm mark) to x 1016 at y 540 with the label 6 mm in 40 px at x 962, y 590; one grey #6B7280 bracket from x 188 to x 908 at y 540 with the label 4 cm in 40 px at x 548, y 590. READ-OUT: across the bottom centre, y 700, one line of bold text 4 cm 6 mm = 46 mm in 64 px. In all: 1 ruler, 61 ticks, 1 line, 2 brackets. All shapes are flat fills with thin dark #2B2B2B outlines (3 px), no shadows and no gradients; all text is dark #1F2937 sans-serif. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
more or fewer than 61 ticks on the ruler
images.takeaway: Read the cm first, then count the small marks: 4 cm 6 mm is 46 mm.
images.description: A ruler from 0 to 6 cm with a line that ends on the 6th small mark after 4 cm, written 4 cm 6 mm = 46 mm.
images.context: Concept image for Reading and Drawing Lengths in cm and mm. It follows the idea of the Let Us Draw lines in your maths book (lengths in cm and mm and in mm) and shows the concept's own example of 4 cm 6 mm.
images.teaching_notes: Count the small marks after the 4 with the child. The slip to watch: reading 4 cm 6 mm as 4 cm 60 mm.
